title: Centennial
name: Centennial
metaDescription: Centennial 1031 exchange guidance for airport-adjacent flex space, corporate office parks, and the redeveloped Streets at SouthGlenn near Denver.

sections.html: Centennial sits south of the Denver Tech Center along the I-25 corridor, and its commercial identity comes from two things: Centennial Airport on the east side and a string of corporate office parks running along Arapahoe Road. It's a younger city than Littleton or Golden, incorporated in 2001, and the building stock reflects that, mostly built from the 1980s through the early 2000s rather than carrying the older mixed vintage found in some other Denver-area submarkets.

sections.heading: How Centennial Airport Changes Nearby Development
sections.html:
Centennial Airport is one of the busiest general aviation airports in the country, mostly corporate and private aircraft rather than commercial airline traffic, and it has pulled in hangar space, aviation services buildings, and executive flex space that you won't find in most other south-metro submarkets. A buyer looking at property near the airport should check for any airport influence overlay zoning, since noise and height restrictions near an active runway are a real constraint that doesn't apply three miles away.

Centennial's boundaries run right up against DTC office towers to the north, and some brokers use the two names loosely enough that a buyer should confirm the actual jurisdiction on any specific parcel rather than trusting a listing's neighborhood label. Property tax rates and permitting timelines can differ between the two even on adjacent parcels.

sections.heading: The Property Types on This List
sections.html:
What actually trades in Centennial:

  • hangar and aviation-services flex space near Centennial Airport
  • corporate office parks along the Arapahoe Road and I-25 corridor
  • mixed-use retail at the redeveloped Streets at SouthGlenn
  • light industrial and distribution buildings on the city's eastern edge

sections.heading: SouthGlenn Is Another Dead-Mall Story
sections.html:
The Streets at SouthGlenn sits on the site of the old SouthGlenn Mall, redeveloped into an open-air mixed-use center with retail, restaurants, and residential above some of the storefronts. It's a similar story to Belmar over in Lakewood, an enclosed mall that got torn down and rebuilt as a walkable town center format, and it now leases better than the aging strip retail nearby along University Boulevard.

Centennial's eastern edge, closer to Peoria Street and the E-470 interchange, carries a growing cluster of distribution and logistics buildings that lease on beltway access the same way similar product does further north in Aurora. That corridor should be underwritten against E-470 industrial comps rather than against the office parks a few miles west along Arapahoe Road.

sections.heading: Diligence Points Specific to Centennial
sections.html: Confirm airport influence overlay zoning on anything within a few miles of Centennial Airport before assuming a proposed use or building height is by-right. On corporate office parks, check occupancy trend the same way a buyer would in DTC, since hybrid work has pulled at suburban office demand across this whole corridor and downtown alike. On distribution buildings near the E-470 interchange, confirm clear height and dock door count against current logistics tenant standards, since older buildings on that edge of the city were built to a smaller specification than a modern e-commerce distribution tenant typically requires.

sections.heading: Positioning a Centennial Identification
sections.html: Aviation-adjacent flex space near the airport is a distinct enough asset class that it usually gets paired with a more conventional office or retail property, a Streets at SouthGlenn parcel or a DTC office building, rather than standing alone on an identification list. That pairing gives an exchange buyer both a niche, less-liquid asset and a more standard, easier-to-finance one. A qualified intermediary should confirm early whether a lender has experience underwriting aviation-adjacent collateral, since not every commercial lender is set up to finance a hangar or aviation-services building the way they would a standard office or retail asset. Rent roll analysis on any Streets at SouthGlenn parcel should separate the redevelopment's original national tenants from more recent backfill leases, since renewal terms and concession packages have shifted noticeably since the center first opened. A replacement property identification for Centennial should note the exact corridor by name in the paperwork, rather than only the city, since airport-adjacent flex space, corporate office, and SouthGlenn retail underwrite as three separate exercises rather than one blended market. A tax advisor coordinating Form 8824 for a Centennial exchange should keep those three asset classes clearly separated on the return, since depreciation schedules and cost segregation treatment differ across hangar flex space, standard office, and retail.

faqs.q: What is airport influence overlay zoning and why does it matter near Centennial Airport?
faqs.a: It restricts building height and use near an active runway for noise and safety reasons. Confirm this zoning before assuming a proposed use or building height is allowed on any parcel near the airport.

faqs.q: Is hangar and aviation-services space a common 1031 replacement property?
faqs.a: It's a real but niche asset class in Centennial, usually less liquid than standard office or retail, so most buyers pair it with a more conventional property rather than using it alone.

faqs.q: How does the Streets at SouthGlenn compare to Belmar in Lakewood?
faqs.a: Similar story, both replaced an enclosed mall with a walkable, mixed-use town center format, and both now lease better than the older strip retail nearby.

faqs.q: Is Centennial office facing the same vacancy pressure as DTC?
faqs.a: Largely yes. Hybrid work has pulled at suburban office demand across the whole I-25 corridor, so check occupancy trend rather than a single current snapshot.

faqs.q: What pairs well with an airport-adjacent Centennial identification?
faqs.a: A Streets at SouthGlenn retail parcel or a DTC office building, giving the exchange a more standard, easier-to-finance asset alongside the niche aviation-related one.
